pains.title: Vaccines: cash out first, paid back later
pains.problem: Practices buy privately purchased vaccines up front and are repaid when claims pay. The AAP reports immunizations are one of the largest practice expenses after payroll.
pains.how: Lucid's cash forecast includes your vaccine orders, and your CPA sets up vaccine purchases as their own cost line. Lucid does not negotiate with payers or run billing.

pains.title: A full schedule and thin profit
pains.problem: Pediatrics is mostly well visits, sick visits and vaccines at fee schedules you cannot change, and Medicaid covers many children at rates that have historically run below Medicare.
pains.how: Lucid reports revenue by payer type and service line and margin by provider and location, with break even scenarios. Your biller and practice system stay in place.

pains.title: Flu season highs and summer lows
pains.problem: Sick visits depend on viral seasons that change every year, while holidays and summer bring a lighter schedule against the same salaries.
pains.how: Lucid builds a rolling cash forecast from your own seasonal history and sets a reserve target for slow months, so you know your low point before it arrives.

faq.q: Why is my pediatric practice busy but not making money?
faq.a: Payers set the price per visit, and Medicaid, which covers many children, has historically paid less than Medicare, while staff, rent and vaccine costs keep rising. Lucid builds monthly books by payer and by service line so you can see what each type of visit earns after overhead, and what volume you need to break even.

faq.q: How should my pediatric practice record vaccines it buys?
faq.a: Vaccines you buy with your own money are a cost to record separately from free publicly supplied vaccine. Your dedicated CPA sets up that cost line.

faq.q: How do I know how much my pediatric practice is owed by insurance?
faq.a: Lucid reports insurance receivable aging by payer and reconciles it to your bank deposits each month. Your biller works the claims.

faq.q: Can my pediatric practice afford another nurse practitioner?
faq.a: It depends on the visits that provider will add and what your payers pay for them. Lucid's CFO scenario planning models the cost of the hire against added collections at your payer mix.

faq.q: How do I see which location of my pediatric group is profitable?
faq.a: You need books where each location has its own revenue, staff cost and rent, with shared costs split by a method you set. Lucid reports margin by location and by provider, so partners can compare sites with the same numbers.
